metadata.case_name: LAU KWAI SHEUNG v. TRADE EASY DEVELOPMENT LTD

source: I am of the view that for a case of a relatively non-violent accident with only soft tissue injury, even if there was some psychological/psychiatric element, a claim of HK$500,000 would be wildly optimistic.

There was also some indication of an “egg skull rule”-type argument regarding the MRI findings of pre-existing spine degeneration, as well as some indication of a psychological/psychiatric explanation of the abnormal “pain behaviour”.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: inconsistent performance during work capacity evaluation by the occupational therapist

treatments_received: orthopaedic assessment by treating orthopaedics doctors

losses.description: Claim that the plaintiff could not work as a waitress but needed to take up her current (allegedly lower paid) job as a cashier (claim for loss of future earnings).

Claim under PSLA in respect of the soft tissue injury with possible psychological/psychiatric element (judge notes a claim of HK$500,000 would be wildly optimistic and a reasonable prospect no more than HK$200,000).
